doc.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Husband Shorty Sherock's band, Quinichette and Freddie Green
summary: Her first husband led a mixed band with Paul Quinichette; Granz's small group dropped Freddie Green, who insisted on staying.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So you saw the Basie band through kind of many manifestations?

Oh, yeah. As a matter of fact my first husband was a musician. Both of my husbands are dead so, too bad they can’t correct anything I’m going to say that’s a mistake. But he had been a jazz trumpet player inspired by Roy Eldridge in his later years, and he formed a little band, and it was a mixed band. And the tenor player was insane about Lester Young. And everybody called him the “Vice Prez,” Paul Quinichette.
And he started with Shorty Sherock’s little orchestra. So then he got, you know, his dream came true, he got to work with Basie too. A lot of wonderful people went through that band.
And for a short time he had a small group too. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

Yes. Well that was a heartbreak at first for him, because I think Norman Granz who was you know a genius about money, I think he thought that the small group would probably pay off better and they eliminated Freddie Green and Basie got apoplectic because that was his heartbeat. And so they finally rectified that.

Well this morning we had Bill Crow. And in his book he tells this little story about shortly after that small group went out that Freddie Green showed up at a gig and just set his stuff up and said “you’re not leaving me behind.”
“I gave you the best years of my life.”
